exams.title: Global Success 12 – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire – Test 1: Ngữ pháp & Từ vựng (15 câu)

qs.q:
UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE — NGỮ PHÁP & TỪ VỰNG (ĐỀ 1): Mark the letter A, B, C, or D on your answer sheet to indicate the correct answer to each of the following questions.
While the military doctor Đặng Thùy Trâm ______ wounded soldiers in Quảng Ngãi, she wrote a famous diary.
qs.ex: Ngữ pháp Unit 1 Lớp 12: Hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ làm nền ('While + Past Continuous: was treating').

qs.q: Steve Jobs ______ out of Reed College after one semester, but continued auditing calligraphy classes.
qs.ex: Sự kiện đã hoàn tất trong quá khứ → Quá khứ đơn: dropped (drop out of = bỏ học giữa chừng).

qs.q: When the American veteran read Đặng Thùy Trâm’s diary while he ______ in Viet Nam, he decided to keep it safe.
qs.ex: Sau 'while' chỉ hành động đang diễn ra trong quá khứ → Quá khứ tiếp diễn: was serving.

qs.q: Steve Jobs was adopted at birth by Paul and Clara Jobs, who promised his ______ parents that he would go to college.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1 Lớp 12: biological parents = cha mẹ ruột.

qs.q: Walt Disney ______ his first animation company in Kansas City, which unfortunately went bankrupt a year later.
qs.ex: Sự việc đã xảy ra và kết thúc trong quá khứ → Quá khứ đơn: started.

qs.q: General Võ Nguyên Giáp is admired around the world for his military ______ and devotion to the nation.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1: military genius = thiên tài quân sự.

qs.q: While Walt Disney ______ on a train from New York to Hollywood, he sketched the first drawings of Mickey Mouse.
qs.ex: Sau 'While' diễn tả hành động dài đang diễn ra trong quá khứ → Quá khứ tiếp diễn: was travelling.

qs.q: At the age of twenty-seven, Đặng Thùy Trâm ______ her youth and life to saving injured soldiers on the battlefield.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1: devote one’s life to V-ing = cống hiến cuộc đời cho...

qs.q: What ______ you ______ when the documentary about Emperor Quang Trung started on VTV1 last night?
qs.ex: Hành động đang diễn ra ('were / doing') tại thời điểm một hành động khác bắt đầu ('when... started') tối qua.

qs.q: Despite being diagnosed with pancreatic ______ in 2003, Steve Jobs continued leading Apple to create the iPhone and iPad.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1 (bài đọc Steve Jobs): pancreatic cancer = bệnh ung thư tuyến tụy.

qs.q: The animated film Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs became a huge ______ and won eight Oscars.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1: blockbuster = bộ phim bom tấn ăn khách.

qs.q: My grandfather ______ the People’s Army of Viet Nam when he was only eighteen years old.
qs.ex: Sự kiện xảy ra tại một mốc tuổi trong quá khứ ('when he was only eighteen') → Quá khứ đơn: joined.

qs.q: Queen Elizabeth I had a strong ______ and ruled England successfully for forty-five years.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1: strong determination = ý chí quyết tâm mạnh mẽ.

qs.q: As the soldiers ______ through the rain forest, they sang patriotic songs to keep their spirits high.
qs.ex: Sau 'As' (= While) chỉ hành động đang diễn ra làm nền → Quá khứ tiếp diễn: were marching.

qs.q: Young people today deeply admire the ______ of frontline doctors who sacrificed their comfort to save lives.
qs.ex: Từ vựng Unit 1: selflessness = lòng vị tha, sự quên mình.

**Read the following leaflet and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the option that best fits each of the numbered blanks from 1 to 6.**

**INSPIRING LIFE STORIES EXHIBITION**
Right now, our school and community **(1)**______ a special campaign focused on admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators, and we invite everyone to join us. Many young readers and historians regularly participate in inspiring biographies in history and modern life, where **(2)**______ a positive difference every week. Taking part in these activities helps young people learn how to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes. Educators and families also note that **(3)**______ inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society. This month, our organisers **(4)**______ practical workshops on how to admire and learn from great life stories, so please **(5)**______ the activities in your neighbourhood. Your active **(6)**______ will help build a better future for everyone!
(Adapted from Global Success – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)
qs.ex: Sau 'While she...' trong câu kể quá khứ → Quá khứ tiếp diễn: was working.

**Dear Alex,**
a. At school, our teachers also organise practical projects to help us learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.

**PERSPECTIVES ON LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
In recent years, admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators has attracted growing attention from educators and researchers alike. A recent national survey reports that while over eighty per cent of young readers and historians recognise the importance of inspiring biographies, only about thirty-five per cent have <u>**admired**</u> these practices into their daily routines in history and modern life. Even when resources are available, many people still struggle to balance their busy schedules with the need to admire and learn from great life stories.
The challenge lies not only in awareness but also in daily habits. Researchers note that active participants regularly engage in structured tasks that learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes, whereas passive observers only join occasional events once or twice a year. Consistent practice requires patience and planning, but it delivers lasting rewards. Many individuals simply repeat outdated habits they observed in the past, which prevents them from experiencing how inspiring biographies can inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society.
Fortunately, attitudes are shifting rapidly. **[I]** Most respondents in the survey agreed that everyone should admire and learn from great life stories, even though many admitted spending less than two hours a week on it themselves. **[II]** Progress was strongest in communities where schools and families worked together as partners. **[III]** Groups can begin by setting clear weekly goals and giving every member a practical role in history and modern life. **[IV]** Small, steady steps like these can turn a difficult challenge into a shared habit of cooperation.
Promoting admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators matters for the long-term future. Young people who see young readers and historians model positive behaviours are likely to view these practices as normal, and <u>**they**</u> will carry those values into adulthood. In this way, inspiring biographies not only learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes today but also inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society for generations to come.
(Adapted from Educational & Social Research Reports – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

Young readers and historians can start with simple steps in history and modern life, share responsibilities and use practical checklists to stay on track. Those who understand the purpose behind admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators become much more resilient and motivated.
Of course, no single workshop or rule will solve every challenge overnight, and some groups need time to adapt. That is no reason to give up. Even one or two focused sessions a week can spark meaningful change, and the positive <u>**achievement**</u> will grow stronger over time. What matters most is the commitment people bring to supporting one another every day.

**PARTNERSHIPS BETWEEN SCHOOLS AND FAMILIES IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Over the past two years, a research team from the National Institute of Education has tracked 1,500 high school students to evaluate how admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators affects teenager development. The study found that while nearly ninety per cent of young readers and historians valued inspiring biographies, only forty-two per cent <u>**sustained**</u> these routines throughout the entire school year. Students who tried to practise alone often gave up after a few weeks when exam pressure increased.
By contrast, learners whose families and teachers coordinated their guidance achieved far more durable results. In households where parents actively joined weekend activities to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life, teenagers were twice as likely to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes. Researchers explained that shared routines reduce the feeling of isolation and turn abstract classroom advice into enjoyable daily habits. Moreover, consistent family involvement helps inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society without adding extra stress to students’ timetables.
Schools across the country are now redesigning their programmes based on these findings. **[I]** Instead of assigning theoretical worksheets, teachers invite parents and students to co-sign a simple weekly action plan. **[II]** This joint commitment ensures that classroom lessons are reinforced at home every evening. **[III]** At monthly review sessions, classes celebrate collective progress and exchange practical solutions to common obstacles. **[IV]**
The long-term implications of this partnership model are encouraging. When young readers and historians work side by side, <u>**they**</u> build mutual respect and lasting life skills. Ultimately, integrating admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators into both school curricula and family life prepares young citizens to thrive in an increasingly complex world.
(Adapted from National Educational Research Reports – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**WHY CONSISTENCY MATTERS MORE THAN PERFECTION IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
When people first decide to focus on admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators, they often set overly ambitious targets. Enthusiastic beginners might promise to transform their entire lifestyle in a single weekend, only to feel exhausted a few days later. Studies on habit formation show that well-paced inspiring biographies are far more effective when built step by step, helping young readers and historians learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes without burnout.
The main reason crash campaigns fail is that <u>**they**</u> demand too much willpower at once. <u>**Small, consistent efforts practised every day produce far more lasting results than occasional bursts of intense activity.**</u> When a routine fits naturally into a family’s or student’s daily schedule, it requires less mental strain to maintain.
Experts therefore recommend a <u>**gradual**</u> approach to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life. By starting with one simple task each day and celebrating weekly milestones, learners steadily build momentum. Such steady practice not only strengthens personal discipline but also helps communities inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society.
Of course, occasional setbacks are normal during busy exam weeks or family events. Rather than abandoning the goal altogether, resilient learners simply resume their routine the next morning, knowing that patience will <u>**foster**</u> long-term success.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**COMMUNITY ACTION AND PEER MENTORING IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Last year, youth unions in three provinces launched a six-month pilot programme to promote admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators at the grassroots level. Instead of relying on formal lectures, organisers trained two hundred high school volunteers to lead weekend activities where neighbours could admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life. Within the first two months, local communities reported <u>**tangible**</u> improvements in daily habits and neighbourhood solidarity.
A key factor behind this success was peer-to-peer mentoring. Teenagers often feel intimidated when adults lecture them, but they respond enthusiastically when classmates demonstrate how inspiring biographies can learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes. By working in small teams of five or six, participants shared practical tips, solved everyday problems together and helped one another inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society.
Organisers also introduced simple tools to keep momentum high. **[I]** Every participating household received a visual progress board to track weekly milestones. **[II]** Local cultural centres hosted monthly gatherings where teams showcased their most creative ideas. **[III]** These celebrations turned routine tasks into a source of shared pride across the entire district. **[IV]**
Follow-up surveys conducted six months later confirmed that over seventy-five per cent of participants continued practising inspiring biographies independently. When student volunteers take ownership of community initiatives, <u>**their**</u> enthusiasm inspires both younger children and older residents. The pilot programme demonstrates that youth-led action is one of the most powerful ways to bring the values of Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire to life.
(Adapted from Community Development & Youth Studies – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**THE RIPPLE EFFECT OF PEER LEADERSHIP IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
How do positive habits spread across a school or neighbourhood? Sociologists studying admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators have discovered that peer influence is often stronger than formal rules. When young readers and historians see their close friends willingly engage in inspiring biographies, they are far more likely to join in and learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
Nevertheless, launching a new initiative is never without challenges. Organisers note that initial doubts and busy routines are common, and <u>**they**</u> can slow down participation during the first week. <u>**Young people learn most effectively when they observe respected peers applying positive habits in real-life situations.**</u>
For this reason, many schools encourage <u>**voluntary**</u> student ambassadors to lead by example. Whether demonstrating how to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life or sharing practical tips during break time, these role models create a welcoming ripple effect that helps the whole school inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society.
Even when a minor <u>**obstacle**</u> arises, a supportive peer group keeps members motivated. What begins as the effort of a few enthusiastic students soon grows into a proud tradition shared by the entire community.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**OVERCOMING BARRIERS TO DAILY PRACTICE IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Why do many high school students agree that admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators is important, yet still find it difficult to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life every day? Educational psychologists point out that modern teenagers face three main barriers: digital distractions, academic pressure and a lack of structured routines. When students feel overwhelmed, they often become <u>**reluctant**</u> to take on new responsibilities at home or in the community.
Fortunately, behavioural research shows that breaking large goals into micro-habits can overcome this hesitation. Instead of trying to change everything overnight, young readers and historians can start with a fifteen-minute daily routine focused on inspiring biographies. These manageable actions quickly build confidence and help learners learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes without interfering with their homework.
Another effective strategy is using a structured weekly checklist. **[I]** When teenagers write down specific times and places for their tasks, they are three times more likely to follow through. **[II]** Sharing <u>**it**</u> with a supportive classmate or family member adds friendly accountability. **[III]** Rather than feeling pressured, students enjoy tracking their streak of completed tasks and seeing how their efforts inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society. **[IV]**
Teachers who have introduced micro-habits and checklists into their lessons on Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire report remarkable improvements in student engagement. Once young people realise that small daily choices lead to meaningful results, inspiring biographies stops feeling like a burden and becomes a natural part of who they are.
(Adapted from Adolescent Psychology & Education Review – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**COMBINING TRADITIONAL VALUES WITH MODERN TOOLS IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
In the digital age, some commentators worry that modern technology might distract young people from admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators. Yet recent educational projects show that when used wisely, digital tools can actually strengthen inspiring biographies. Shared mobile calendars, reminder apps and online group checklists make it easier than ever for young readers and historians to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
Of course, technology alone cannot solve every problem. Researchers warn against relying passively on apps while ignoring face-to-face communication, as <u>**they**</u> are only tools in the hands of users. <u>**Digital tools should serve as a practical bridge to support daily cooperation rather than a replacement for genuine human interaction.**</u>
When families and classmates combine smart reminders with warm personal encouragement, they can <u>**preserve**</u> the core spirit of Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire. For example, a quick evening message can remind everyone to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life before gathering for a friendly conversation.
Ultimately, blending modern convenience with timeless values helps communities <u>**enhance**</u> their daily routines and inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society in a sustainable way.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND THE FUTURE OF UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Across Viet Nam, forward-thinking high schools are transforming how students learn about admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators. Rather than treating Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire as a set of vocabulary items to memorise for a test, teachers are integrating experiential learning into every week of the semester. Educators agree that hands-on practice is <u>**indispensable**</u> if young people are to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
In these classrooms, students work in project teams to investigate real issues and propose ways to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life. For instance, learners might interview local residents, design bilingual awareness posters or organise a school-wide campaign on inspiring biographies. Through these authentic tasks, young readers and historians discover how their classroom English connects directly to everyday life.
Assessment methods are evolving alongside teaching styles. **[I]** Instead of relying solely on written quizzes, schools evaluate how effectively students collaborate and apply their plans. **[II]** Each team keeps a reflective portfolio documenting the challenges they faced and how their actions helped inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society. **[III]** This approach rewards creativity, persistence and genuine teamwork rather than rote memorisation. **[IV]**
Graduates of experiential programmes consistently report higher confidence when entering university and the workplace. Students <u>**who**</u> have practised solving real-world problems in high school adapt much faster to new environments. By making admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators an active, lived experience, education equips the next generation with both language proficiency and civic responsibility.
(Adapted from Modern Curriculum & Pedagogy Journal – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**Read the passage and mark the letter A, B, C or D on your answer sheet to indicate the best answer to each of the following questions from 17 to 26.**

**EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING AND THE FUTURE OF UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Across Viet Nam, forward-thinking high schools are transforming how students learn about admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators. Rather than treating Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire as a set of vocabulary items to memorise for a test, teachers are integrating experiential learning into every week of the semester. Educators agree that hands-on practice is <u>**indispensable**</u> if young people are to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
In these classrooms, students work in project teams to investigate real issues and propose ways to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life. For instance, learners might interview local residents, design bilingual awareness posters or organise a school-wide campaign on inspiring biographies. Through these authentic tasks, young readers and historians discover how their classroom English connects directly to everyday life.
Assessment methods are evolving alongside teaching styles. **[I]** Instead of relying solely on written quizzes, schools evaluate how effectively students collaborate and apply their plans. **[II]** Each team keeps a reflective portfolio documenting the challenges they faced and how their actions helped inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society. **[III]** This approach rewards creativity, persistence and genuine teamwork rather than rote memorisation. **[IV]**
Graduates of experiential programmes consistently report higher confidence when entering university and the workplace. Students <u>**who**</u> have practised solving real-world problems in high school adapt much faster to new environments. By making admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators an active, lived experience, education equips the next generation with both language proficiency and civic responsibility.
(Adapted from Modern Curriculum & Pedagogy Journal – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

**SELF-REFLECTION AND LONG-TERM GROWTH IN UNIT 1: LIFE STORIES WE ADMIRE**
Practising inspiring biographies is even more rewarding when learners take a few minutes each week to reflect on their progress. Educators studying admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators have found that students who keep a brief weekly journal understand their own habits much better and find it easier to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
During busy weeks, people sometimes miss a planned task or make mistakes. Without reflection, <u>**they**</u> may feel discouraged and assume that their efforts have failed. <u>**Honest self-reflection allows learners to turn early mistakes into valuable lessons rather than reasons to give up.**</u>
To make reflection effective, teachers recommend asking <u>**constructive**</u> questions every Sunday evening: What went well when we tried to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life this week, and what small adjustment will help us improve next week?
Over time, this simple habit deepens personal <u>**commitment**</u> and helps young readers and historians inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society with confidence and pride.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)

It requires learners to write fifty pages every night.

Educators studying admiring inspiring life stories, national heroes and innovators have found that students who keep a brief weekly journal understand their own habits much better and find it easier to learn about the determination and selflessness of national heroes.
During busy weeks, people sometimes miss a planned task or make mistakes. Without reflection, <u>**they**</u> may feel discouraged and assume that their efforts have failed. <u>**Honest self-reflection allows learners to turn early mistakes into valuable lessons rather than reasons to give up.**</u>
To make reflection effective, teachers recommend asking <u>**constructive**</u> questions every Sunday evening: What went well when we tried to admire and learn from great life stories in history and modern life this week, and what small adjustment will help us improve next week?
Over time, this simple habit deepens personal <u>**commitment**</u> and helps young readers and historians inspire teenagers to overcome obstacles and contribute to society with confidence and pride.
(Adapted from Global Success Reading Series – Unit 1: Life Stories We Admire)
